title: iTransformer: Inverted Transformers Are Effective for Time Series Forecasting
grouping: Two rows, existing approach on top ('Transformer View', red label) and proposed below ('iTransformer View', blue label), joined by a purple downward chevron labelled 'Invert'. Each row is a series plot on the left, a hollow arrow, and a 3-D token pipeline on the right ending in a rotated representation label.
shapes_depth: Three variates are line plots in cyan, teal and yellow on Value/Time axes. Top: red vertical bars cross all three curves at time steps, each topped with 'Token' and marked with grey dots where it meets a curve. Bottom: each whole curve sits in its own blue dashed box labelled 'Token'. The right side uses columns of 3-D cubes: grey cubes with one red-outlined token column in the top row; cubes coloured by variate with one blue-outlined token row in the bottom row; attention is a translucent beige box and the FFN translucent light-blue slabs. Double-headed arrows name the axes (Time Steps / Embedding vs Variates / Embedding).
proposed_highlight: Red marks the baseline's token and blue the proposed one, in the row labels, the token outlines and the words 'Mixed' / 'Unmixed' in the output labels; the variate colours survive into the cubes only in the proposed row, while the baseline's cubes are grey.
lesson: Contrast two tokenizations on the same drawn curves (a vertical bar across all variates at one time step vs a dashed box around one whole variate) and keep the variate colours in the 3-D token cubes only for the proposed row, with grey cubes meaning mixed.
notes: Venue and year from the PDF header (ICLR 2024). The paper's Figure 1 could not be cropped (no caption found).

measured.source: computed: paperfig kb measure (non-white pixels of a <= 800 px thumbnail, white = min(R,G,B) >= 245, minus the embedded images recorded by `refs crop` (images_px; their share is photo_share, null without a record); chromatic (RGB spread > 20) and neutral pixels clustered separately by PIL median-cut + k-means (k=8 / 3); clusters within dE00 4 merged; kept if >= 0.02 of chromatic pixels / neutral ones if >= 0.03 of all non-white pixels; share = fraction of the non-photo non-white pixels)

core.what: Transformer view (top) and iTransformer view (bottom) as two identical rows, joined by a purple 'Invert' arrow, each pairing the tokenized series on the left with its 3-D token stack, attention and FFN on the right

relations.form: two rows with the same layout (series plot, hollow arrow, cube stack, attention box, FFN slabs, output cubes), prior on top and ours below, a big purple downward 'Invert' arrow between their labels
tokens are drawn on the series plots themselves: red vertical bars across all three curves at single time steps (top) versus blue dashed boxes around each whole curve (bottom)
in each row left to right on the right side: embedded token cubes, a translucent beige attention volume, translucent blue FFN slabs, then the output representation cubes

channels.colour: curve colours (light blue, teal, yellow) = the three variates, carried into the bottom row's cubes so 'unmixed' is visible, while the top row's cubes are grey = mixed; red vs blue also mark the two views and their token outlines, so red/blue carry view while the variate palette carries identity
channels.shape: cubes = embedded token entries; translucent box = attention; stacked translucent slabs = FFN; curves = raw series
channels.line: hollow block arrows = data into the model; black double arrows label the Embedding / Time Steps / Variates axes
channels.frame: red outline = one temporal token, blue dashed outline = one variate token

quality.strengths: The inversion is pure geometry: the same pipeline drawn twice, tokens cut vertically across time in one and horizontally per series in the other, and the representations are drawn as cube stacks whose colour shows variate-mixed (grey) versus variate-unmixed (per-variate colours).
quality.weaknesses: Attention and FFN are blank translucent volumes with no indication of what attends to what; the 3-D cubes are ink-heavy and the axis arrows (Embedding, Time Steps, Variates) crowd the first stack.

insights.structure: Two stacked rows contrast the vanilla Transformer view (top) with the iTransformer view (bottom), joined by a purple 'Invert' arrow on the left; each row pairs a multivariate line plot with a 3-D cube pipeline of attention and FFN.
insights.data: Inputs are three coloured time-series curves; tokens are red vertical bars across time (top) vs dashed boxes around each whole series (bottom); representations are stacks of coloured cubes, grey for mixed and teal/gold per variate for unmixed.
insights.emphasis: Colour carries the argument: red marks the time-step token and 'Mixed', blue marks the variate token and 'Unmixed', and the bottom row keeps per-variate colours through the cubes while the top row turns grey.
insights.flow: Each row reads left-to-right from plot through a hollow arrow into embed, attention slab, FFN slabs and output cubes; the eye compares the rows vertically.
insights.avoid: The translucent attention and FFN slabs are nearly identical between rows, so the difference relies on small rotated labels and cube colours.

arrangement.units: two unenclosed rows (Transformer view, iTransformer view), each a plot followed by a 3-D cube pipeline
arrangement.inputs_as: multivariate line plots with token markings
arrangement.shared: same pipeline order (embedding, attention, FFN, representation) in both rows
